claims.title: How historical parameters and the visibility refactor were checked
claims.conclusion: Historical parameters were compared using values from the same file across different commits; differences between Home Mixer and VM Ranker within the same commit were listed separately. Static checks covered conditions, call paths, index writes and reads, version differences, and formulas. The original report also states that an earlier examination of the latest visibility refactor expanded and compared 14 groups of rule lists and fields. The exact named groups and retained comparison result for that historical count have not been independently reconstructed. These were structural checks; the production safety service was not run.

claims.title: Historical assertion groups must not be combined and presented as official integration tests
claims.conclusion: The original research retained results for 143 assertions from Python reimplementations of ranking and filtering, including consistency checks against 26 source files. The earlier manuscript-writing stage separately recorded 22 local assertions and checks against 8 source files for candidate counting, long/short interleaving, conversation display, and deduplication, as well as 14 weighted assertions and checks against 4 source files for reposts and dwell. These groups differ in scope; their counts must not be added together and advertised as that many official integration tests. This report revision read the results from the original verification package and did not present historical records as if all checks had been rerun in this round.

claims.title: The verification scope of local functions, numeric results, and miniature simulations
claims.conclusion: Numeric boundaries, time loss, and some output forms came from earlier CPU checks that directly called the original Python/JAX functions or extracted unchanged pure functions. Those checks alone cannot establish the physical units of production events; upstream gaps concerning the CLICK_DWELL_TIME threshold of 10 and the definition of Article reading were retained following the supplementary checks in this report revision. Attention checks included self-built miniature computations, and ranking examples included mathematical reimplementations; neither is equivalent to running the complete production model. This report revision also rechecked source code for the author multiplier, cold-start eligibility, FairShare, dwell loss, media truncation, and related parameters, and recalculated the main numerical examples in the text.

claims.title: An official recommendation score cannot be calculated from arbitrary body text
claims.conclusion: The named model output `CLICK_DWELL_TIME` has been traced through to the service response; the complete adapter that converts it into the identically named Home Mixer field has still not been found. Production model weights, some prompts, upstream event definitions, and per-request configurations have not been fully disclosed, so a credible “official recommendation score” cannot be calculated for arbitrary body text. The research also did not sign in to a user account to verify whether Under the Hood was available, or conduct real-account growth or causal exposure experiments.

claims.title: Code facts, examples, and editorial advice have different roles
claims.conclusion: The character scenarios, price-quote copy, OCR drafts, and fixed-probability worked examples in the text are all illustrative. Parameters and eligibility are code facts; how to arrange the lead image, schedule updates, and choose topics are editorial suggestions based on those facts, and their effects still require actual reader data.

claims.title: The scope of the Article candidate and visibility search
claims.conclusion: The Article/long Post investigation in this report revision also examined Home Mixer sources, filters, scorers, params, and candidate_pipeline, along with related types, visibility, and action interfaces. The candidate and visibility portion retained a bounded search record covering 103 files; the events portion recorded gaps between protocols, training reads, historical features, service conversions, and aggregation services. The search found no dedicated format multiplier, which does not prove that external services or undisclosed experiments have no format preferences.

claims.title: V5 and V8.2 function checks and cross-version comparisons
claims.conclusion: A further 10 direct function checks were performed on the V5/V8.2 content processors, and all passed. The tests used lightweight in-memory objects with populated fields and substituted environment dependencies. They did not call the embedding service, load model weights, or simulate exposure. Of the 14 content-path files compared, 12 had identical blobs across the two commits; the other two files only added organization-badge image fields, leaving the relevant Article mappings unchanged. The number of earlier numeric assertions does not increase because of this textual revision, and these function checks are not described as a live format experiment.
